```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE)
library(readxl); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(stringr); library(ggplot2)
```

# Purpose

Collapse the 12 per-image binary columns of every condition block down to **one summary
variable per participant per condition**, and apply the regulador / perturbador
classification rule to each sound + oral condition.

Three rules, one per block type, applied to every block found in the workbook:

| Block type | Rule |
|---|---|
| Sound-only (`E1`) | `1` if any of the 12 images shows a 1, else `0` |
| Sound + oral (`E2`-`E12`) | `regulador` / `perturbador` / `no clasificado`, relative to that participant's own sound-only result |
| Oral alone, no sound (`E13`-`E23`) | `1` if any of the 12 images shows a 1, else `0`, plus a Spanish label |

**Descriptive only. No inferential statistics are run here and none may be run until
`ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` is agreed** — see §10 of that file, where this script is logged. The
classification is a *re-description* of the raw grid, not a test.

⚠️ Two properties of the classification rule govern how its output may be read. They are
stated here because the numbers below are meaningless without them, and repeated in
`ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` §2a.8-9.

1. **Both labels condition on a single, unrepeated measurement of `E1`.** Regulador selects
   participants who read positive under sound and asks whether they later read negative;
   perturbador selects those who read negative and asks whether they later read positive.
   Under pure response instability, with no stimulus effect whatever, both groups are
   non-empty by construction. `E1` was presented once, so that instability is not estimable
   from this file.
2. **The two criteria are not equally exposed to that instability.** Regulador requires *all
   12* images to read 0 — a conjunction of 12 events. Perturbador requires *any 1 of 12* to
   read 1 — a disjunction. The perturbador rate therefore runs higher than the regulador
   rate for arithmetic reasons alone. **The two counts have different denominators, are not
   comparable to each other, and must never be summed.** Both denominators are carried in
   every output below so that cannot happen silently.

# Load

The workbook is read-only source. It is copied out before reading, never opened in place.

```{r load}
raw_dir <- file.path("..", "..", "data", "raw")
xl <- list.files(raw_dir, pattern = "\\.xlsx$", full.names = TRUE)
stopifnot(length(xl) == 1)

# The workbook is often open in Excel, and then cannot be read in place by any ordinary
# route. readable_copy() falls through three of them; see src/readable_copy.R.
source("readable_copy.R")

xlc <- readable_copy(xl)

# Sheet row 1 is a merged group header naming each condition block; row 2 carries the column
# names. skip = 1 makes row 2 the header.
d <- read_excel(xlc, sheet = "Datos", skip = 1)
names(d)[1:4] <- c("row_index", "pid", "sex", "age")

cat("participants:", nrow(d), " columns:", ncol(d), "\n")
```

# 1. Condition block inventory

The set of blocks is read **from the workbook**, not hardcoded, so a block added to the file
appears here rather than being silently dropped.

Row 1 is read back at exactly the width of the data so the two rows stay index-aligned, then
the merged group-header labels are filled forward across the columns they span — which is
what a merged cell means.

```{r inventory}
gh <- as.character(unlist(read_excel(
  xlc, sheet = "Datos", col_names = FALSE, .name_repair = "minimal",
  range = cell_limits(c(1, 1), c(1, ncol(d)))
)))
stopifnot(length(gh) == ncol(d))

# fill merged group-header labels forward
for (i in seq_along(gh)) {
  if (is.na(gh[i]) || trimws(gh[i]) == "") gh[i] <- if (i > 1) gh[i - 1] else NA_character_
}

grid_idx  <- 5:ncol(d)
grid_cols <- names(d)[grid_idx]

blocks <- tibble(
  col   = grid_cols,
  label = gh[grid_idx],
  # "ESTIMULO 2 = M1 + SONIDO" -> number 2, condition "M1 + SONIDO"
  e_hdr = as.integer(str_match(label, "(?i)EST[ÍI]MULO\\s*(\\d+)")[, 2]),
  cond  = str_trim(str_match(label, "=\\s*(.*)$")[, 2]),
  # the column's own name carries the condition number too: "IM3 E2"
  im    = as.integer(str_match(col, "^IM\\s*(\\d+)")[, 2]),
  e_col = as.integer(str_match(col, "E(\\d+)$")[, 2])
)

# The two independent sources of the condition number must agree for every column. If a block
# were mis-spanned in the sheet, or the columns were out of order, this is where it surfaces.
mismatch <- filter(blocks, is.na(e_hdr) | is.na(e_col) | e_hdr != e_col)
if (nrow(mismatch)) {
  print(mismatch)
  stop(nrow(mismatch), " columns where the group header and the column name disagree ",
       "about which condition they belong to")
}
stopifnot(all(!is.na(blocks$im)), all(blocks$im %in% 1:12))

inventory <- blocks |>
  group_by(e = e_col, cond) |>
  summarise(n_images = n(), images = paste0("IM", min(im), "-IM", max(im)), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(
    block_type = case_when(
      str_detect(cond, "(?i)^solo\\s+sonido$") ~ "sound_only",
      str_detect(cond, "(?i)\\+\\s*SONIDO$")   ~ "oral_plus_sound",
      TRUE                                      ~ "oral_alone"
    ),
    # the oral stimulus identity, shared by a with-sound block and its no-sound counterpart
    oral = if_else(block_type == "sound_only", NA_character_,
                   str_trim(str_remove(cond, "(?i)\\s*\\+\\s*SONIDO$"))),
    type = case_when(
      block_type == "sound_only" ~ "Sound",
      oral %in% c("M1", "M2", "M3") ~ "COS",
      TRUE ~ "DS"
    )
  ) |>
  arrange(e)

# Every block must be a full 12 images, and every block type must be represented.
stopifnot(all(inventory$n_images == 12))
stopifnot(sum(inventory$block_type == "sound_only") == 1)

knitr::kable(inventory, caption = "Condition blocks found in the workbook")

cat("\nblocks:", nrow(inventory),
    "| sound-only:", sum(inventory$block_type == "sound_only"),
    "| sound + oral:", sum(inventory$block_type == "oral_plus_sound"),
    "| oral alone:", sum(inventory$block_type == "oral_alone"), "\n")
cat("binary cells:", nrow(d) * nrow(inventory) * 12, "\n")
```

⚠️ **There is no baseline (no-stimulus) block.** The grid begins at `E1` = sound. The
paper's 0/38 at baseline is not in this file and cannot be rebuilt from it
(`ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` §2a.5).

Every sound + oral block must have a no-sound counterpart with the same oral stimulus, or the
phase-4 follow-up in §5 has nothing to match against.

```{r pairing}
paired <- inventory |>
  filter(block_type != "sound_only") |>
  select(e, oral, block_type) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = block_type, values_from = e)

stopifnot(!any(is.na(paired$oral_plus_sound)), !any(is.na(paired$oral_alone)))
knitr::kable(paired, caption = "Each oral stimulus, with sound and without")
```

# 2. Validate the grid

```{r validate}
vals <- unlist(d[grid_cols])
cat("distinct values in the grid:", paste(sort(unique(vals)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("missing cells:", sum(is.na(vals)), "\n")
stopifnot(all(vals %in% c(0, 1)))

stopifnot(!any(is.na(d$pid)), !anyDuplicated(d$pid))
cat("participant key unique:", nrow(d), "rows,", n_distinct(d$pid), "distinct IDs\n")
cat("sex 1=male 2=female:", paste(names(table(d$sex)), table(d$sex), sep = "="), "\n")
cat("age: mean", round(mean(d$age), 1), "SD", round(sd(d$age), 1),
    "range", min(d$age), "-", max(d$age), "\n")
```

# 3. Collapse each block to one value per participant

```{r collapse}
long_cell <- d |>
  select(pid, sex, age, all_of(grid_cols)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(grid_cols), names_to = "col", values_to = "vs") |>
  left_join(select(blocks, col, e = e_col, im), by = "col")

stopifnot(nrow(long_cell) == nrow(d) * nrow(inventory) * 12)

# one row per participant x condition
by_cond <- long_cell |>
  group_by(pid, sex, age, e) |>
  summarise(n_im = sum(vs), any_vs = as.integer(n_im > 0), .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(select(inventory, e, cond, block_type, oral, type), by = "e")

stopifnot(nrow(by_cond) == nrow(d) * nrow(inventory))
cat("condition-level rows:", nrow(by_cond), "\n")
```

# 4. Classify each sound + oral condition

The rule, per participant and per sound + oral condition, against that participant's own
sound-only result:

- **regulador** — `any_vs == 1` under sound alone **and** all 12 images read 0 under
  sound + oral.
- **perturbador** — `any_vs == 0` under sound alone **and** at least one image reads 1 under
  sound + oral.
- **no clasificado** — everything else. Not forced into either label.

`no clasificado` merges two situations that are not the same thing, so the reason is kept in
its own column rather than lost:

| `class_reason` | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `vs_en_ambas` | VS under sound alone **and** still VS under sound + oral — includes partial improvement, no change, and worsening |
| `sin_vs_en_ninguna` | no VS under either condition — the stimulus had nothing to change |

⚠️ Note what the rule cannot see. A participant with VS under sound whose VS *spreads to more
images* under sound + oral is `vs_en_ambas` — the same cell as no change at all. Because
eligibility for each label is fixed by `E1`, **a participant can never be both regulador and
perturbador.** That mutual exclusivity is a property of the rule, not a finding about two
participant types.

```{r classify}
sound_only <- by_cond |>
  filter(block_type == "sound_only") |>
  select(pid, vs_sound = any_vs, n_im_sound = n_im)

stopifnot(nrow(sound_only) == nrow(d))

classified <- by_cond |>
  left_join(sound_only, by = "pid") |>
  mutate(
    class_reason = case_when(
      block_type != "oral_plus_sound"        ~ NA_character_,
      vs_sound == 1 & any_vs == 0            ~ "regulador",
      vs_sound == 0 & any_vs == 1            ~ "perturbador",
      vs_sound == 1 & any_vs == 1            ~ "vs_en_ambas",
      vs_sound == 0 & any_vs == 0            ~ "sin_vs_en_ninguna"
    ),
    classification = factor(
      case_when(
        block_type != "oral_plus_sound" ~ NA_character_,
        class_reason %in% c("regulador", "perturbador") ~ class_reason,
        TRUE ~ "no clasificado"
      ),
      levels = c("regulador", "perturbador", "no clasificado")
    ),
    vs_label = if_else(any_vs == 1, "escotoma presente", "escotoma no presente")
  )

stopifnot(!any(is.na(classified$class_reason[classified$block_type == "oral_plus_sound"])))
```

## The two denominators

Eligibility for each label is decided entirely by the sound-only column, so the denominators
are fixed before any oral stimulus is considered.

```{r denominators}
n_total  <- nrow(sound_only)
n_sound  <- sum(sound_only$vs_sound == 1)   # eligible to be regulador
n_nosnd  <- sum(sound_only$vs_sound == 0)   # eligible to be perturbador
stopifnot(n_sound + n_nosnd == n_total)

cat("participants:", n_total, "\n")
cat("VS under sound alone  -> eligible for REGULADOR only:  ", n_sound, "\n")
cat("no VS under sound alone -> eligible for PERTURBADOR only:", n_nosnd, "\n")
```

## Counts per condition

```{r counts-per-condition}
# A label with no occurrences anywhere would otherwise be an absent column rather than a zero,
# and every downstream reference to it would fail. Guarantee all of them.
ensure_cols <- function(df, cols) {
  for (cn in cols) if (!cn %in% names(df)) df[[cn]] <- 0L
  df
}

counts <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |>
  count(e, oral, type, classification) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = classification, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  ensure_cols(c("regulador", "perturbador", "no clasificado")) |>
  left_join(
    classified |>
      filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |>
      count(e, class_reason) |>
      pivot_wider(names_from = class_reason, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
      ensure_cols(c("vs_en_ambas", "sin_vs_en_ninguna")) |>
      select(e, vs_en_ambas, sin_vs_en_ninguna),
    by = "e"
  ) |>
  mutate(
    n_eligible_regulador  = n_sound,
    n_eligible_perturbador = n_nosnd,
    pct_regulador   = round(100 * regulador / n_sound, 1),
    pct_perturbador = round(100 * perturbador / n_nosnd, 1)
  ) |>
  arrange(e)

knitr::kable(counts, caption = paste0(
  "Classification by sound + oral condition. Percentages use different denominators: ",
  "regulador of ", n_sound, ", perturbador of ", n_nosnd, "."
))
```

## Participant-level rollup

Whether each participant was *ever* classified either way across the eleven sound + oral
conditions. This is the level the manuscript reports at.

```{r rollup}
rollup <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  summarise(
    vs_sound          = first(vs_sound),
    n_regulador       = sum(classification == "regulador"),
    n_perturbador     = sum(classification == "perturbador"),
    ever_regulador    = as.integer(n_regulador > 0),
    ever_perturbador  = as.integer(n_perturbador > 0),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

cat("ever regulador:  ", sum(rollup$ever_regulador), "of", n_sound, "eligible\n")
cat("ever perturbador:", sum(rollup$ever_perturbador), "of", n_nosnd, "eligible\n")
cat("both (impossible by construction):", sum(rollup$ever_regulador & rollup$ever_perturbador), "\n")
stopifnot(sum(rollup$ever_regulador & rollup$ever_perturbador) == 0)
```

### Cross-check against the published elimination endpoint

The regulador rule is, word for word, the "elimination of sound-induced VS" endpoint already
rebuilt in `reconcile_published_counts.Rmd` — VS under sound alone, then no VS in any of the
12 drawings once an oral stimulus is added. So the participant-level regulador count must
reproduce the published **18 of 23**. If it does not, one of the two scripts is wrong.

```{r crosscheck}
cat("regulador (participant level):", sum(rollup$ever_regulador), "/", n_sound, "\n")
cat("published elimination endpoint: 18 / 23\n")

if (sum(rollup$ever_regulador) == 18 && n_sound == 23) {
  cat("MATCH - the regulador rule is the published elimination endpoint.\n")
} else {
  cat("*** MISMATCH - reconcile before anything downstream uses this. ***\n")
}
```

# 5. Does the oral stimulus disrupt without sound?

The phase-4 follow-up on the perturbador classifications: where an oral stimulus induced a VS
*with* sound present, did **the same stimulus** induce one with the sound off?

Matched on the oral stimulus, not on a `+11` offset, so it stays correct if the block order
changes.

```{r phase4}
oral_alone <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_alone") |>
  select(pid, oral, vs_alone = any_vs, n_im_alone = n_im)

perturb_follow <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound", classification == "perturbador") |>
  select(pid, oral, e, n_im_with_sound = n_im) |>
  left_join(oral_alone, by = c("pid", "oral"))

stopifnot(!any(is.na(perturb_follow$vs_alone)))

cat("perturbador classifications (participant x stimulus):", nrow(perturb_follow), "\n")
if (nrow(perturb_follow) > 0) {
  cat("  ...of which the same stimulus alone, no sound, also induced a VS:",
      sum(perturb_follow$vs_alone), "\n")
}

knitr::kable(
  perturb_follow |>
    count(oral, vs_alone) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = vs_alone, values_from = n, values_fill = 0,
                names_prefix = "vs_alone_") |>
    arrange(oral),
  caption = "Perturbador classifications, by whether the same oral stimulus disrupted without sound"
)
```

⚠️ This follow-up selects a subgroup on a noisy criterion and then re-tests it in a phase that
**always came later** (`ANALYSIS_PLAN.md` §2a.1), with no comparison group and no correction.
It can only ever confirm. It is reported as a description of what those participants did, and
carries no inferential weight.

# 6. Outputs

## Wide summary — one row per participant

```{r write-wide}
safe <- function(x) str_replace_all(str_to_lower(str_replace_all(x, "[ +]+", "_")),
                                   "[^a-z0-9_]", "")

col_for <- function(e, cond, suffix = "") {
  paste0("E", e, "_", safe(cond), suffix)
}

snd <- filter(inventory, block_type == "sound_only")
wide_sound <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "sound_only") |>
  select(pid, any_vs)
names(wide_sound)[2] <- col_for(snd$e, snd$cond)

wide_class <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |>
  select(pid, e, cond, classification) |>
  mutate(name = col_for(e, cond, "_class")) |>
  select(pid, name, classification) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = classification)

wide_alone_bin <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_alone") |>
  select(pid, e, cond, any_vs) |>
  mutate(name = col_for(e, cond, "_vs")) |>
  select(pid, name, any_vs) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = any_vs)

wide_alone_lab <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_alone") |>
  select(pid, e, cond, vs_label) |>
  mutate(name = col_for(e, cond, "_vs_label")) |>
  select(pid, name, vs_label) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = name, values_from = vs_label)

summary_wide <- d |>
  transmute(pid, sex, sex_label = if_else(sex == 1, "hombre", "mujer"), age) |>
  left_join(wide_sound,     by = "pid") |>
  left_join(wide_class,     by = "pid") |>
  left_join(wide_alone_bin, by = "pid") |>
  left_join(wide_alone_lab, by = "pid") |>
  arrange(pid)

stopifnot(nrow(summary_wide) == nrow(d), !any(is.na(summary_wide)))

proc <- file.path("..", "..", "data", "processed")
dir.create(proc, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(summary_wide, file.path(proc, "participant_condition_summary.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

cat("participant_condition_summary.csv:", nrow(summary_wide), "x", ncol(summary_wide), "\n")
knitr::kable(summary_wide[1:6, 1:9], caption = "Wide summary, first 6 participants")
```

## Long form — one row per participant x condition

The analysis substrate: this is the shape a model is fitted to, and it carries the reason
column and the labels.

```{r write-long}
summary_long <- classified |>
  transmute(
    pid, sex, sex_label = if_else(sex == 1, "hombre", "mujer"), age,
    e, condition = cond, block_type, oral, type,
    n_im, any_vs, vs_label,
    vs_sound, classification, class_reason
  ) |>
  arrange(pid, e)

write.csv(summary_long, file.path(proc, "participant_condition_long.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("participant_condition_long.csv:", nrow(summary_long), "x", ncol(summary_long), "\n")
```

## Classification counts table

```{r write-counts}
tab <- file.path("..", "outputs", "tables")
dir.create(tab, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
write.csv(counts, file.path(tab, "condition_classification_counts.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

write.csv(rollup, file.path(tab, "participant_classification_rollup.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
cat("wrote condition_classification_counts.csv and participant_classification_rollup.csv\n")
```

# 7. Figure

## Colour decisions

Recorded because they are choices, not defaults, and continuous with
`vs_matrices_and_heatmaps.Rmd`.

**Regulador vs perturbador is a polarity, not two nominal categories** — one label is a VS
removed, the other a VS induced — so it takes a **diverging pair**: one cool pole, one warm,
never two arbitrary hues and never red/green. `#2a78d6` is the blue already used for "VS
present" in the existing heatmaps, kept so the two figures read as one system; `#c2610f` is
its warm counterpart.

Validated with the `dataviz` palette validator against surface `#fcfcfb`: lightness band,
chroma floor, CVD separation and contrast all pass, worst adjacent pair ΔE **26.5** under
protanopia and **30.5** at normal vision — far above the ΔE 8 target. The pair also separates
on lightness, so it survives greyscale printing.

**No legend, because the panel headings name the two labels.** Identity is therefore carried
by text rather than by colour, which is what the accessibility rule actually asks for; a
legend as well would be pure redundancy. Counts are direct-labelled on every bar and the same
numbers are in `condition_classification_counts.csv`, so no value is reachable only by colour.

**Two panels rather than two bars per stimulus.** The two counts share a unit but not a
denominator, and a shared axis would invite the reader to compare bar lengths across labels —
the one comparison this classification does not license.

```{r figure, fig.width=9, fig.height=6, dpi=300}
col_regulador   <- "#2a78d6"
col_perturbador <- "#c2610f"
surface     <- "#fcfcfb"
ink_muted   <- "#898781"
ink_primary <- "#0b0b0b"

plot_dat <- counts |>
  select(oral, type, regulador, perturbador) |>
  pivot_longer(c(regulador, perturbador), names_to = "label", values_to = "n") |>
  mutate(
    # Small multiples, not two bars on one axis. The counts share a unit (participants) but
    # NOT a denominator, so putting them on one shared axis would invite exactly the
    # length-comparison the caption has to forbid. Each panel carries its own denominator.
    panel = factor(
      if_else(label == "regulador",
              paste0("Regulador — of the ", n_sound, " with a pseudo-scotoma under sound alone"),
              paste0("Perturbador — of the ", n_nosnd, " without one")),
      levels = c(paste0("Regulador — of the ", n_sound,
                        " with a pseudo-scotoma under sound alone"),
                 paste0("Perturbador — of the ", n_nosnd, " without one"))
    ),
    oral_f = factor(oral, levels = rev(counts$oral))   # workbook order, top to bottom
  )

p_class <- ggplot(plot_dat, aes(n, oral_f, fill = label)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.62, colour = surface, linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_text(aes(label = n), hjust = -0.4, size = 2.9, colour = ink_muted) +
  facet_wrap(~ panel) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(regulador = col_regulador, perturbador = col_perturbador),
                    guide = "none") +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
  labs(
    title    = "Regulador and perturbador classifications, by oral stimulus",
    subtitle = paste0("Participants classified under each of the 11 oral stimuli, ",
                      "sound maintained. n = ", n_total, ".\n",
                      "The two panels have different denominators and are not comparable ",
                      "to each other."),
    x = "Participants classified", y = "Oral stimulus",
    caption = paste0(
      "Panels are separated because they do not share a denominator: eligibility for each ",
      "label is fixed by the sound-only condition,\n",
      "so the ", n_sound, " participants who could be classified regulador and the ", n_nosnd,
      " who could be classified perturbador are disjoint groups.\n",
      "Regulador also requires all 12 images to clear, while perturbador requires only 1 of 12 ",
      "to appear, so perturbador counts run higher for arithmetic reasons alone.\n",
      "Descriptive re-description of the raw grid; no test is implied. ",
      "Values in outputs/tables/condition_classification_counts.csv"
    )
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.minor   = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "#e8e6e2", linewidth = 0.3),
    panel.spacing.x    = unit(18, "pt"),
    strip.text         = element_text(colour = ink_primary, face = "bold", size = 8.5),
    axis.text          = element_text(colour = ink_muted),
    axis.title         = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 9),
    plot.title         = element_text(colour = ink_primary, face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle      = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 8.5),
    plot.caption       = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 7, hjust = 0),
    plot.background    = element_rect(fill = surface, colour = NA)
  )
p_class

fig <- file.path("..", "outputs", "figures")
dir.create(fig, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
ggsave(file.path(fig, "classification_by_oral_stimulus.png"), p_class,
       width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```

# 8. Heatmaps

## Colour decisions for the classification states

Red for perturbador and green for regulador are **Esther's choice, 2026-08-17**, and are used
as asked. They come with a cost that has to be paid rather than ignored:

`#cf222e` against `#2da44e` measures **ΔE 7.2 under deuteranopia and 6.4 under tritanopia** —
inside the 6–8 floor band, where a categorical pair is legal *only* if colour is not the sole
carrier of the distinction. Roughly one man in twelve cannot reliably separate that pair, on
cells whose entire job is separating three states. So **every classified cell carries a letter
glyph — `R` for regulador, `P` for perturbador, blank for neither** — and the state is
readable with the colour discarded entirely. At normal vision the pair is ΔE 33.5, so the
figure is vivid for everyone else. This is the documented relief, not a workaround.

The sound and oral-alone cells keep the existing blue/neutral pair (ΔE 37.8), which needs no
secondary encoding, and grey `#b8b5ae` holds "neither" — a neutral by intent, which is why it
does not meet the chroma floor a categorical hue would.

```{r heat-palette}
col_vs_present <- "#2a78d6"   # blue   - VS present (sound, oral alone)
col_vs_absent  <- "#f0efec"   # light neutral - no VS
col_regulador  <- "#2da44e"   # green  - Esther's choice
col_perturbador<- "#cf222e"   # red    - Esther's choice
col_neither    <- "#b8b5ae"   # grey   - neither label

state_levels <- c("VS present", "No VS", "Regulador", "Perturbador", "Neither")
state_cols <- c("VS present"  = col_vs_present, "No VS"       = col_vs_absent,
                "Regulador"   = col_regulador,  "Perturbador" = col_perturbador,
                "Neither"     = col_neither)

oral_order <- inventory |> filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |> arrange(e) |> pull(oral)

theme_heat <- theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(
    panel.grid      = element_blank(),
    panel.spacing.x = unit(16, "pt"),
    strip.clip      = "off",
    axis.text.x     = element_text(angle = 90, vjust = 0.5, hjust = 1, colour = ink_muted),
    axis.text.y     = element_text(size = 6.5, colour = ink_muted),
    axis.title      = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 9),
    strip.text      = element_text(colour = ink_primary, face = "bold", size = 9),
    plot.title      = element_text(colour = ink_primary, face = "bold", size = 12),
    plot.subtitle   = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 8.5),
    plot.caption    = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 7, hjust = 0),
    plot.background = element_rect(fill = surface, colour = NA),
    legend.title    = element_blank(),
    legend.text     = element_text(colour = ink_muted, size = 8)
  )

gap <- 0.35   # tile borders drawn in the surface colour ARE the gap between marks
```

Row order is shared by all three heatmaps so they can be read against each other: sound
responders first (the block where regulador can occur), then by how many stimuli were
regulador, then perturbador.

```{r heat-order}
ord <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  summarise(vs_sound = first(vs_sound),
            n_reg  = sum(classification == "regulador"),
            n_pert = sum(classification == "perturbador"), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(vs_sound), desc(n_reg), desc(n_pert))

pid_levels <- rev(ord$pid)
cat("row order: ", sum(ord$vs_sound == 1), " sound-responders on top, then ",
    sum(ord$vs_sound == 0), "\n", sep = "")
```

## Sound, and the classification under sound + oral

```{r heatmap-classification, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, dpi=300}
heat_a <- classified |>
  filter(block_type %in% c("sound_only", "oral_plus_sound")) |>
  mutate(
    state = case_when(
      block_type == "sound_only" & any_vs == 1 ~ "VS present",
      block_type == "sound_only" & any_vs == 0 ~ "No VS",
      classification == "regulador"            ~ "Regulador",
      classification == "perturbador"          ~ "Perturbador",
      TRUE                                     ~ "Neither"
    ),
    glyph = case_when(state == "Regulador" ~ "R", state == "Perturbador" ~ "P", TRUE ~ ""),
    panel = factor(if_else(block_type == "sound_only", "Sound alone", "Oral + sound"),
                   levels = c("Sound alone", "Oral + sound")),
    col_f = factor(if_else(block_type == "sound_only", "Sound", oral),
                   levels = c("Sound", oral_order)),
    pid_f = factor(pid, levels = pid_levels),
    state = factor(state, levels = state_levels)
  )

p_heat_a <- ggplot(heat_a, aes(col_f, pid_f, fill = state)) +
  geom_tile(colour = surface, linewidth = gap) +
  geom_text(aes(label = glyph), size = 2, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  facet_grid(. ~ panel, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_cols, drop = FALSE) +
  labs(
    title    = "Sound response, and how each oral stimulus changed it",
    subtitle = paste0("Sound alone: was there a pseudo-scotoma? Oral + sound: regulador (R), ",
                      "perturbador (P) or neither, against that\nparticipant's own sound-only ",
                      "result. n = ", n_total, "; each cell collapses 12 drawings."),
    x = NULL, y = "Participant",
    caption = paste0(
      "R and P are printed in every classified cell because red and green sit at ",
      "deltaE 7.2 under deuteranopia - the state is readable without colour.\n",
      "Eligibility is fixed by the sound column: only the ", n_sound,
      " participants with a pseudo-scotoma under sound can be regulador, only the ", n_nosnd,
      " without can be perturbador.\n",
      "'Neither' merges no-change, partial improvement AND worsening. Rows ordered by sound ",
      "response, then regulador count. Values in data/processed/participant_condition_long.csv"
    )
  ) +
  theme_heat
p_heat_a

ggsave(file.path(fig, "heatmap_sound_and_classification.png"), p_heat_a,
       width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```

## The oral stimuli alone, without sound

```{r heatmap-oral-alone, fig.width=9, fig.height=8, dpi=300}
heat_b <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_alone") |>
  mutate(
    state = factor(if_else(any_vs == 1, "VS present", "No VS"), levels = state_levels),
    col_f = factor(oral, levels = oral_order),
    pid_f = factor(pid, levels = pid_levels)
  )

p_heat_b <- ggplot(heat_b, aes(col_f, pid_f, fill = state)) +
  geom_tile(colour = surface, linewidth = gap) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_cols, drop = TRUE, limits = c("VS present", "No VS")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Pseudo-scotoma under each oral stimulus alone, no sound",
    subtitle = paste0("Headphones on, sound off. Same participants and same row order as the ",
                      "previous figure, so the two can be read\nagainst each other. n = ",
                      n_total, "; each cell collapses 12 drawings."),
    x = NULL, y = "Participant",
    caption = paste0(
      "No classification applies here: regulador and perturbador are defined only against ",
      "the sound-only condition.\n",
      "This phase always ran last, so a difference from the previous figure is confounded ",
      "with time, fatigue and practice (ANALYSIS_PLAN.md 2a.1).\n",
      "Values in data/processed/participant_condition_long.csv"
    )
  ) +
  theme_heat
p_heat_b

ggsave(file.path(fig, "heatmap_oral_alone_vs.png"), p_heat_b,
       width = 9, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```

## Elimination only, in the 23 sound-responders

Added 2026-08-18 for the client summary, which reports the elimination endpoint and does not
report `perturbador`. This figure is the elimination endpoint and nothing else: rows are the
`r sum(sound_only$vs_sound == 1)` participants who reported a pseudo-scotoma under sound alone
— the only people for whom "elimination" is a question — and each oral cell is a two-state
answer.

Restricting the rows is what removes `perturbador` from the figure entirely: the label is
defined only for participants with **no** VS under sound, and none of them is in this figure.
So no cell here is ambiguous and no legend entry goes unused.

```{r heatmap-elimination, fig.width=9, fig.height=6.5, dpi=300}
elim_pids <- sound_only |> filter(vs_sound == 1) |> pull(pid)
stopifnot(length(elim_pids) == n_sound)

elim_order <- classified |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound", pid %in% elim_pids) |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  summarise(n_elim = sum(classification == "regulador"), .groups = "drop") |>
  arrange(desc(n_elim))

col_eliminated <- "#2da44e"   # green - VS cleared, Esther's choice, kept from the R/P figure
elim_levels <- c("VS present", "Eliminated", "VS persists")
elim_cols <- c("VS present" = col_vs_present, "Eliminated" = col_eliminated,
               "VS persists" = col_vs_present)

heat_e <- classified |>
  filter(pid %in% elim_pids, block_type %in% c("sound_only", "oral_plus_sound")) |>
  mutate(
    state = case_when(
      block_type == "sound_only"  ~ "VS present",
      classification == "regulador" ~ "Eliminated",
      TRUE                          ~ "VS persists"
    ),
    glyph = if_else(state == "Eliminated", "E", ""),
    panel = factor(if_else(block_type == "sound_only", "Sound alone", "Sound + OPS"),
                   levels = c("Sound alone", "Sound + OPS")),
    col_f = factor(if_else(block_type == "sound_only", "Sound", oral),
                   levels = c("Sound", oral_order)),
    pid_f = factor(pid, levels = rev(elim_order$pid)),
    state = factor(state, levels = elim_levels)
  )

# The figure must carry the published endpoint, or it is not the figure it claims to be.
n_ever_elim <- heat_e |>
  filter(block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  summarise(any_e = any(state == "Eliminated"), .groups = "drop") |>
  summarise(k = sum(any_e)) |>
  pull(k)
stopifnot(n_ever_elim == 18, n_sound == 23)

p_heat_e <- ggplot(heat_e, aes(col_f, pid_f, fill = state)) +
  geom_tile(colour = surface, linewidth = gap) +
  geom_text(aes(label = glyph), size = 2.2, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  facet_grid(. ~ panel, scales = "free_x", space = "free_x") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = elim_cols, breaks = c("VS present", "Eliminated"),
                    labels = c("Pseudo-scotoma present", "Pseudo-scotoma eliminated (E)")) +
  labs(
    title    = "Elimination of sound-induced pseudo-scotomas, by individual oral stimulus",
    subtitle = paste0("The ", n_sound, " participants who reported a pseudo-scotoma under sound ",
                      "alone. Green indicates that the pseudo-scotoma was\nabsent from all 12 ",
                      "drawings under that stimulus while the sound was maintained. ",
                      n_ever_elim, " of ", n_sound,
                      " participants responded to at least\none stimulus, and the effective ",
                      "stimulus differed between individuals."),
    x = NULL, y = "Participant",
    caption = paste0(
      "OPS = oral proprioceptive stimuli. M1-M3 are combined oral stimuli; the remaining ",
      "eight are dental stimuli, labelled by tooth (FDI notation)\n",
      "and site (V = buccal, P = palatal, L = lingual). E is printed in every green cell so ",
      "that the two states are distinguishable without colour.\n",
      "Participants are ordered by the number of effective stimuli; the five participants at ",
      "the foot responded to none. Blue merges no change,\n",
      "partial improvement and worsening. The sound condition was presented once, so the rate ",
      "at which a pseudo-scotoma resolves\n",
      "spontaneously on re-testing could not be estimated."
    )
  ) +
  theme_heat +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank())
p_heat_e

ggsave(file.path(fig, "heatmap_elimination.png"), p_heat_e,
       width = 9, height = 6.5, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```

### The same endpoint collapsed across the eleven stimuli

Added 2026-08-18. Same 23 participants and same row order as the figure above, reduced to the
question the published endpoint asks: **did *any* oral stimulus clear it?** Two states, nothing
else printed in the cells.

⚠️ **This figure is written for the manuscript**, so the caption carries no path, no filename and
no cross-reference to the analysis plan — a reader of the paper cannot follow any of those. The
one caveat that must survive is the opportunity asymmetry, and it is stated in words a journal
reader can act on.

```{r heatmap-elimination-collapsed, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=6.5, dpi=300}
elim_collapsed <- classified |>
  filter(pid %in% elim_pids, block_type == "oral_plus_sound") |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  summarise(n_elim = sum(classification == "regulador"), .groups = "drop") |>
  transmute(
    pid,
    `Sound alone` = "VS present",
    `Sound + OPS` = if_else(n_elim > 0, "Eliminated", "VS persists")
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-pid, names_to = "col", values_to = "state") |>
  mutate(
    state = factor(state, levels = elim_levels),
    col_f = factor(col, levels = c("Sound alone", "Sound + OPS")),
    pid_f = factor(pid, levels = rev(elim_order$pid))
  )

stopifnot(sum(elim_collapsed$state == "Eliminated") == 18)

p_elim_c <- ggplot(elim_collapsed, aes(col_f, pid_f, fill = state)) +
  geom_tile(colour = surface, linewidth = gap) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = elim_cols, breaks = c("VS present", "Eliminated"),
                    labels = c("Pseudo-scotoma present", "Pseudo-scotoma eliminated")) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(
    title    = "Elimination of sound-induced pseudo-scotomas",
    subtitle = paste0("Each row is one of the ", n_sound, " participants who reported a ",
                      "pseudo-scotoma under sound\nalone. Green indicates that the ",
                      "pseudo-scotoma was absent from all 12 drawings\nunder at least one OPS ",
                      "condition while the sound was maintained (", n_ever_elim, "/", n_sound,
                      "; 78.3%)."),
    x = NULL, y = "Participant",
    caption = paste0(
      "OPS = oral proprioceptive stimuli. The OPS column summarises 11 stimulus conditions,\n",
      "whereas the sound condition was presented once; the two columns therefore differ in\n",
      "the number of opportunities for a pseudo-scotoma to be recorded and are not a\n",
      "like-for-like comparison. Blue in the right-hand column merges no change, partial\n",
      "improvement and worsening."
    )
  ) +
  theme_heat +
  theme(legend.title = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x  = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = 8.5))
p_elim_c

ggsave(file.path(fig, "heatmap_elimination_collapsed.png"), p_elim_c,
       width = 6.5, height = 6.5, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```

## Collapsed across stimuli — three columns

Each participant reduced to one value per condition type. The collapse rules are Esther's:
any regulador → regulador; any perturbador → perturbador; any VS under an oral stimulus
alone → VS present.

**The two classification rules cannot collide.** Eligibility is fixed by `E1`, so a
participant who can be regulador can never be perturbador, whatever the eleven stimuli did.
That is asserted below rather than assumed — if it ever fails, the collapse is ambiguous and
the figure is wrong.

```{r heatmap-collapsed, fig.width=7, fig.height=8, dpi=300}
collapsed <- classified |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  summarise(
    sound_vs = first(any_vs[block_type == "sound_only"]),
    any_reg  = any(classification[block_type == "oral_plus_sound"] == "regulador"),
    any_pert = any(classification[block_type == "oral_plus_sound"] == "perturbador"),
    oral_vs  = as.integer(any(any_vs[block_type == "oral_alone"] == 1)),
    .groups  = "drop"
  )

stopifnot(!any(collapsed$any_reg & collapsed$any_pert))
stopifnot(nrow(collapsed) == n_total)

cat("collapsed: VS under sound", sum(collapsed$sound_vs), "| any regulador",
    sum(collapsed$any_reg), "| any perturbador", sum(collapsed$any_pert),
    "| VS under any oral stimulus alone", sum(collapsed$oral_vs), "\n")

heat_c <- collapsed |>
  transmute(
    pid,
    `Sound\nalone` = if_else(sound_vs == 1, "VS present", "No VS"),
    `Sound + oral\n(any stimulus)` = case_when(any_reg ~ "Regulador",
                                               any_pert ~ "Perturbador",
                                               TRUE ~ "Neither"),
    `Oral alone\n(any stimulus)` = if_else(oral_vs == 1, "VS present", "No VS")
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(-pid, names_to = "col", values_to = "state") |>
  mutate(
    glyph = case_when(state == "Regulador" ~ "R", state == "Perturbador" ~ "P", TRUE ~ ""),
    state = factor(state, levels = state_levels),
    col_f = factor(col, levels = c("Sound\nalone", "Sound + oral\n(any stimulus)",
                                   "Oral alone\n(any stimulus)")),
    pid_f = factor(pid, levels = pid_levels)
  )

p_heat_c <- ggplot(heat_c, aes(col_f, pid_f, fill = state)) +
  geom_tile(colour = surface, linewidth = gap) +
  geom_text(aes(label = glyph), size = 2.4, colour = "white", fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_cols, drop = FALSE) +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top") +
  labs(
    title    = "One value per participant per condition type",
    subtitle = paste0("Collapsed across the eleven oral stimuli. n = ", n_total, "."),
    x = NULL, y = "Participant",
    caption = paste0(
      "Collapse rules: any regulador -> regulador; any perturbador -> perturbador;\n",
      "any pseudo-scotoma under an oral stimulus alone -> VS present.\n",
      "A participant can never be both labels, because eligibility is fixed by the\n",
      "sound column, so the middle column is never ambiguous.\n",
      "The middle column is a disjunction over 11 stimuli x 12 drawings = 132 binary\n",
      "cells; see ANALYSIS_PLAN.md 2a.9 before reading a rate off it.\n",
      "Values in data/processed/participant_condition_summary.csv"
    )
  ) +
  theme_heat +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 0, hjust = 0.5, vjust = 1, size = 7.5))
p_heat_c

ggsave(file.path(fig, "heatmap_collapsed_three_conditions.png"), p_heat_c,
       width = 7, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```

## Collapsed presence only — the three phases side by side

Added 2026-08-18 for the client summary, which reports prevalence and does not report
`perturbador`. Same three columns as the figure above, but every cell answers the **same**
yes/no question, so the three phases are read on one scale and no cell carries a classification.

**The three phases are separated into their own panels** rather than sitting as three adjacent
columns, so the eye does not read them as one continuous block, and the phase name sits above its
own column instead of on a crowded axis. Also written for the manuscript: no internal paths or
plan references in the caption.

```{r heatmap-collapsed-presence, fig.width=6.5, fig.height=8, dpi=300}
phase_labels <- c("Sound alone", "Sound + OPS", "OPS only")

presence_c <- classified |>
  group_by(pid) |>
  summarise(
    `Sound alone` = first(any_vs[block_type == "sound_only"]),
    `Sound + OPS` = as.integer(any(any_vs[block_type == "oral_plus_sound"] == 1)),
    `OPS only`    = as.integer(any(any_vs[block_type == "oral_alone"] == 1)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

col_totals <- colSums(presence_c[-1])
stopifnot(col_totals == c(23, 34, 31), names(presence_c)[-1] == phase_labels)
pct <- round(100 * col_totals / n_total, 1)

heat_p <- presence_c |>
  pivot_longer(-pid, names_to = "phase", values_to = "vs") |>
  mutate(
    state   = factor(if_else(vs == 1, "VS present", "No VS"), levels = state_levels),
    phase_f = factor(phase, levels = phase_labels),
    pid_f   = factor(pid, levels = pid_levels)
  )

p_presence <- ggplot(heat_p, aes(x = 1, y = pid_f, fill = state)) +
  geom_tile(colour = surface, linewidth = gap) +
  # One panel per phase, so the phases are visibly separate blocks with the name on top.
  facet_grid(. ~ phase_f) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = state_cols, breaks = "VS present",
                    labels = "Pseudo-scotoma reported") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = NULL, expand = expansion(0)) +
  labs(
    title    = "Prevalence of visual pseudo-scotomas by experimental phase",
    subtitle = paste0("One value per participant per phase (n = ", n_total, "). Sound alone ",
                      col_totals[1], "/", n_total, " (", pct[1], "%); sound + OPS ",
                      col_totals[2], "/", n_total, " (", pct[2], "%);\nOPS only ", col_totals[3],
                      "/", n_total, " (", pct[3], "%)."),
    x = NULL, y = "Participant",
    caption = paste0(
      "OPS = oral proprioceptive stimuli. The sound + OPS and OPS only phases each comprise\n",
      "11 stimulus conditions, whereas sound alone was presented once; the phase totals\n",
      "therefore reflect the number of conditions applied as well as the stimuli themselves,\n",
      "and are not a like-for-like comparison. The OPS only phase was always performed last,\n",
      "so differences between phases are confounded with time, fatigue and practice."
    )
  ) +
  theme_heat +
  theme(legend.title    = element_blank(),
        panel.spacing.x = unit(22, "pt"),
        strip.text      = element_text(colour = ink_primary, face = "bold", size = 9.5))
p_presence

ggsave(file.path(fig, "heatmap_vs_binary_collapsed.png"), p_presence,
       width = 6.5, height = 8, dpi = 300, bg = surface)
```
